judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header link "Cymraeg" to the site's Welsh hub (/cy/cymraeg/, title "Cymraeg - General Osteopathic Council", Welsh content). The page is lang="en-GB" and neither the link nor its p ancestor has a lang attribute in the snapshot, so the Welsh word inherits English: claimTrue yes. I looked for a reason it could pass: the proper-name and vernacular exceptions. Understanding 3.1.2 settles it the other way: its example "Alternative language links" (links whose text is the name of the language in that language, e.g. Deutsch, Français) says the language of each link is indicated via a lang attribute; "Cymraeg" is not an adopted English word that English speech rules pronounce correctly. elementFails yes. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same markup (Cymraeg, no lang) and the rendered snapshot shows no script adding one: captureDiffers no. The claim names exactly this failure: true positive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is Google Maps' focusable map viewport: div role="region" aria-label="Map" with aria-roledescription "map" in the accessibility tree and aria-describedby pointing to the keystroke table (arrows move, +/- zoom, Home/End/Page Up/Page Down jump). The snapshot records it as focusable with keydown/keyup/keypress listeners and the region role, so the sentence's facts hold: claimTrue yes. For 4.1.2 the element has a programmatically determined role (region, described as "map"), a name ("Map") and a description of how to operate it. It is a pannable viewport, operated like a keyboard-scrollable area, for which a focusable named region is the recognised pattern; it is neither a button nor a link, so the roles the claim asks for would misdescribe it. F59 covers a div made into a control with no role at all, which is not the case here: elementFails no. The live raw HTML loads the same Google Maps API into #map-practices, so users get the same widget: captureDiffers no. The rule demanded a button/link role that WCAG does not require for this widget: false positive.
